On-boom build with Ø8 mm passive elements on a 20 × 20 mm boom. The published element lengths already include the 3.9 mm boom correction. The half lengths assume a 10 mm gap and a driven element mounted in the plane of the other elements. Published gain at 144.300 MHz is 10.2 dBi for the Ø8 mm model.

The author specifies a 500 mm boom. The element positions span 470 mm from reflector to director. Published gain is 4.72 dBd and front-to-back ratio is 16.5 dB. The series guide gives a typical feed gap of 10–12 mm and states the element lengths tip to tip. The short build uses removable halves. Their blanks depend on the connectors.
Broadband 50 Ω version for 430–440 MHz. The author lists 8.7 dBd gain and specifies a choke with three turns of RG-178 on Ø20 mm PVC.

For a 50 Ω feed, the author uses two 75 Ω quarter-wave sections in parallel. Published length per section is 120 mm for RG-179 (VF 0.70), 115 mm for solid PE, and 141 mm for foam PE (VF 0.82). Published gain at 432.000 MHz is 9.1 dBd.

Type 1 uses one feed point for both bands. The 70 cm open-sleeve element is 22 mm from the driven element. The author gives 4.1 dBd at 145.000 MHz and 5.4 dBd at 435.000 MHz for the 2+2 design. Those values describe the published design. Import your measurements separately for 144–146 and 430–440 MHz.

The mounting table is for Ø8 mm passive elements on a 20 × 20 mm boom with standard insulators. The lengths already include the 6.83 mm correction. The reflector-to-D4 span is 2358 mm. With 40 mm at each end, the boom is 2438 mm long. The published 970.83 mm is the table value for the driven element. The cut list uses the DG7YBN calculator with a 10 mm gap and a bend of about 12.8°. Check final geometry by measuring SWR. The author’s model gives 11.9 dBi at 144.100 MHz.
Schematic top view. Each bend is 100 mm from the feed centre. The tips point towards the reflector and are approximately 188 mm from it along the boom. The drawing shows the feed gap schematically.
The source leaves some blank lengths unspecified. See the notes in this record.

Top view. Each bend is 100 mm from the feed centre. The driven-element tips are 186 mm from the reflector along the boom. The feed gap is schematic.

The cut list gives starting tube lengths for a 10 mm feed gap and a bend of about 12.7°. The on-boom build uses the 6.83 mm correction in the mounting table. The through-boom build uses 8.84 mm. Check final geometry by measuring SWR.
Enter the gap between the metal ends in your mount. Use 10 mm as a starting point for a trial build. The length of each half is (published span − gap) / 2.

Enter the gap between the metal ends, the distance from feed centre to the bend and the tip setback towards the reflector along the boom. Cut lengths are calculated separately for H and V. Check the assembled antenna by measuring SWR.
Model estimates for a 10 mm gap. H: bend at 103 mm, setback 83 mm, blank about 482 mm. V: bend at 100 mm, setback 82 mm, blank about 483 mm.
Enter a valid dimension. The gap can be up to 100 mm and must leave room before the bend. The bend must be within the half-span and the setback within the distance to the reflector.
